comparison.objective: Candidate tunes and mechanically locks a damper to produce safe repeatable stops; pr-827 calibrates a tool center point by holding one tip at a common point from four orientations.
comparison.physical_skill: Candidate combines recessed hex-key insertion, bounded loosening/tightening, collar rotation, counterholding, and response-driven iteration. pr-827 emphasizes precise point contact, wrist reorientation, and one-second static holds.
comparison.success_condition: Candidate requires two non-bottoming cycles and retained adjustment after a witness-torque test. pr-827 requires four contact poses with specified lean, angular separation, contact force/position, and stillness. Candidate lacks numeric rebound, overload, drift, and torque thresholds.
comparison.reason: Both concern robot commissioning and precision control, but they test different abilities: mechanical damper tuning and retention versus invariant-tip kinematic calibration.
